title: PM2
definition: A production process manager for Node.js applications with a built-in load balancer. It allows you to keep applications alive forever, reload them without downtime, and facilitate common system admin tasks.
simpleExplanation: If you start your app with `node index.js` and it crashes, the server is dead until you log in and restart it. PM2 is the ultimate babysitter. You start the app with `pm2 start index.js`. If the app crashes at 3:00 AM, PM2 instantly restarts it in 1 millisecond. It also handles clustering automatically.
realWorldExample: Running `pm2 start server.js -i max`. This single command tells PM2 to look at your server, see it has 8 CPU cores, clone your app 8 times, and balance the traffic between them perfectly.

basic: What does PM2 do if your Node application crashes?

answers.question: What if it crashes?
answers.answer: It automatically restarts the process instantly.

answers.question: What is Zero-Downtime Reload?
answers.answer: When you push new code to your server, you normally have to shut it down for 5 seconds to restart it. If you have 4 clustered instances, PM2 restarts Instance 1 while 2, 3, and 4 keep serving users. It rotates through them so the server never actually goes offline during the update.
